mukta-m0-p08-v176.quick_english: Because the individual self has changeability and similar properties, and because scripture also contradicts it, such a view cannot hold for the individual self.

mukta-m0-p08-v177.quick_english: Thus the individual self is not all-pervading, not momentary, not one, and not inert in nature.

mukta-m0-p08-v178.quick_english: Other groups among the principles are enjoyers and serve as grounds of pleasure.

mukta-m0-p08-v179.quick_english: This means they are the places of enjoyment for transmigrating beings.

mukta-m0-p08-v180.quick_english: The range from hell up to the world of truth is governed by the Kālāhāṭaka lords.

mukta-m0-p08-v181.quick_english: And the Śatarudra lord also governs together with five octads.

mukta-m0-p08-v182.quick_english: But Kalā is governed by the Maṇḍalins.

mukta-m0-p08-v183.quick_english: And one should place them in sequence in the intellect.

mukta-m0-p08-v184.quick_english: But when the state of the qualities has not yet been attained, it should be placed in the pure summit of the qualities.

mukta-m0-p08-v185.quick_english: The row of worlds of Krodheśvara and the other Rudras abides in Pradhāna.

mukta-m0-p08-v186.quick_english: Mahāmāyā is the seed of the world, a productive power, and unconscious.

mukta-m0-p08-v187.quick_english: This Mahāmāyā is endowed with many variegated powers.

mukta-m0-p08-v188.quick_english: Because it is unconscious and multiple, its perishability is well established.

mukta-m0-p08-v189.quick_english: Because souls are infinite, it is all-pervading and acts for the sake of their enjoyment.

mukta-m0-p08-v190.quick_english: It undergoes transformation, but not in its whole nature; by the maxim of the ghee-worm, it should be understood to transform by one part.

mukta-m0-p08-v191.quick_english: Creation, maintenance, and dissolution of that Mahāmāyā are declared to abide within its own nature.

mukta-m0-p08-v192.quick_english: As a means of enjoyment it is the material cause; thus there is no contradiction.

mukta-m0-p08-v193.quick_english: Creation and maintenance have been explained; dissolution is the reversal of creation.

mukta-m0-p08-v194.quick_english: This means reabsorption into their respective causes in the reverse order of creation.

mukta-m0-p08-v195.quick_english: For souls, the object of enjoyment is made of Māyā and is experienced indeed through means born of Māyā.

mukta-m0-p08-v196.quick_english: Also because limited knowledge and such properties are not directly perceived.

mukta-m0-p08-v197.quick_english: Because, when covered by impurity, its all-knowledge and all-action are obscured, it becomes an object.

mukta-m0-p08-v198.quick_english: In the revered Svāyaṃbhuva it is asked: if the soul had no impurity, what would cause its attachment to enjoyments?

mukta-m0-p08-v199.quick_english: Karma performed in another birth gives rise to birth and other fruits for human beings.

mukta-m0-p08-v200.quick_english: The power of karma that produces birth and so forth does not operate without impurity.

mukta-m0-p09-v201.quick_english: Because the performance of action is not seen otherwise, the acquisition of karma and its experience apply only to the soul that is endowed with impurity.

mukta-m0-p09-v202.quick_english: Indeed, let that soul’s object-directedness be one; what use is there for that karma?

mukta-m0-p09-v203.quick_english: There are isolated souls, deprived of karma, whose knowledge is consumed.

mukta-m0-p09-v204.quick_english: The meaning is: the cause lies in connection with māyā.

mukta-m0-p09-v205.quick_english: Because before creation the soul is without parts yet possesses the qualities of cognition and action.

mukta-m0-p09-v206.quick_english: The meaning is that, because connection with kalā would otherwise be inexplicable, impurity must be admitted for that soul.

mukta-m0-p09-v207.quick_english: Because the individual self is omnipresent, its cognition and action are held to have all objects as their scope.

mukta-m0-p09-v208.quick_english: Because there are no manifestors such as kalā and the rest, that soul’s cognition and action are not manifest.

mukta-m0-p09-v209.quick_english: Impurity is in a beginningless connection with the beginningless, is common, and is imperishable.

mukta-m0-p09-v210.quick_english: For that very reason, impurity must indeed be admitted as eternal.

mukta-m0-p09-v211.quick_english: Before the arising of great delusion, this individual self was stainless.

mukta-m0-p09-v212.quick_english: The connection of impurity with the self must be admitted to be beginningless.

mukta-m0-p09-v213.quick_english: O wise ones, if the connection between the soul and impurity is accepted as having a beginning—

mukta-m0-p09-v214.quick_english: Then, if that connection is without cause, the connection with kalā would also be without cause.

mukta-m0-p09-v215.quick_english: And if a beginningless connection between beginningless entities is accepted, can it be perishable?

mukta-m0-p09-v216.quick_english: And its powers, fixed for each soul, obstruct the soul’s qualities.

mukta-m0-p09-v217.quick_english: They obstruct the soul’s quality whose nature is knowledge and action; and this has indeed been shown previously.

mukta-m0-p09-v218.quick_english: Otherwise, all conscious beings would be liberated simultaneously.

mukta-m0-p09-v219.quick_english: Thus, according to the revered Svāyambhuva and other scriptures, they are to be known as indeed adventitious.

mukta-m0-p09-v220.quick_english: The five modifications of object-directedness, beginning with pride, are not proper.

mukta-m0-p09-v221.quick_english: But there is no contradiction, since they have impurity as their material cause.

mukta-m0-p09-v222.quick_english: It is not proper to say that they are manifested merely through connection with the means of experience.

mukta-m0-p09-v223.quick_english: But according to you, pride and the rest are indeed distinct from the modifications of the guṇas.

mukta-m0-p09-v224.quick_english: In due order, two are tāmasa, one is sāttvika, and two are rājasa.

mukta-m0-p09-v225.quick_english: The modifications are not distinct from these; therefore, as modifications distinct from the root, they do not exist.

mukta-m0-p08-v176.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v176.question: Why do changeability and scripture contradict certain views of the individual self?
premises: The individual self has changeability and similar properties.
Such properties create contradiction in the individual self.
Scripture also contradicts those views about the individual self.
mukta-m0-p08-v176.inference: Therefore views incompatible with changeability and scripture cannot correctly describe the individual self.

mukta-m0-p08-v177.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v177.question: Which mistaken characterizations of the individual self must be rejected?
premises: The individual self is not all-pervading.
The individual self is not momentary and not one.
The individual self is not inert-natured.
mukta-m0-p08-v177.inference: Therefore these characterizations do not properly define the individual self.

mukta-m0-p08-v178.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v178.question: How are certain other groups among the principles characterized as enjoyers?
premises: Among the principles there are other groups.
These groups are described as enjoyers.
These groups are grounds of pleasure.
mukta-m0-p08-v178.inference: Therefore some groups of principles function as enjoying grounds.

mukta-m0-p08-v179.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v179.question: What is the intended meaning of the pleasure grounds for transmigrating beings?
premises: The preceding groups were called grounds of pleasure.
Transmigrating beings require places for enjoyment.
The statement is explained as having this meaning.
mukta-m0-p08-v179.inference: Therefore those grounds are the places of enjoyment for transmigrating beings.

mukta-m0-p08-v180.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v180.question: Which range of worlds is governed by the Kālāhāṭaka lords?
premises: A range of worlds is specified.
That range begins with hell.
That range ends with the world of truth.
mukta-m0-p08-v180.inference: Therefore the Kālāhāṭaka lords govern the worlds from hell up to the world of truth.

mukta-m0-p08-v181.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v181.question: Who accompanies the Śatarudra lord in governing the next domain?
premises: The Śatarudra lord is included in the hierarchy.
He is associated with accompanying groups.
Those groups are five octads.
mukta-m0-p08-v181.inference: Therefore the Śatarudra lord governs together with five octads.

mukta-m0-p08-v182.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v182.question: Which lords are assigned governance over the principle Kalā?
premises: The principle Kalā is specified as a domain.
A distinct group of lords is named.
Those lords are the Maṇḍalins.

mukta-m0-p08-v183.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v183.question: How should placement be performed in relation to the intellect?
premises: A placement is being prescribed.
The locus of placement is the intellect.
The placement must follow a sequence.
mukta-m0-p08-v183.inference: Therefore one should place in sequence in the intellect.

mukta-m0-p08-v184.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v184.question: Where should placement occur when the state of qualities is not yet attained?
premises: A state of unattained qualities is considered.
A pure locus is specified.
That locus is the summit of the qualities.
mukta-m0-p08-v184.inference: Therefore placement in that case is at the pure summit of the qualities.

mukta-m0-p08-v185.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v185.question: Where does the row of worlds of Krodheśvara and other Rudras abide?
premises: There is a row of worlds belonging to Krodheśvara and other Rudras.
That row has a specific locus.
That locus is Pradhāna.
mukta-m0-p08-v185.inference: Therefore the row of worlds of Krodheśvara and others abides in Pradhāna.

mukta-m0-p08-v186.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v186.question: What essential nature characterizes Mahāmāyā as the seed of the world?
premises: Mahāmāyā is the seed of the world.
Mahāmāyā is a productive power.
Mahāmāyā is unconscious.
mukta-m0-p08-v186.inference: Therefore Mahāmāyā is an unconscious productive seed of the world.

mukta-m0-p08-v187.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v187.question: How is Mahāmāyā endowed with manifold and diverse powers?
premises: Mahāmāyā possesses powers.
Those powers are many.
Those powers are variegated.
mukta-m0-p08-v187.inference: Therefore Mahāmāyā is endowed with many diverse powers.

mukta-m0-p08-v188.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v188.question: Why is perishability firmly established for Mahāmāyā?
premises: Mahāmāyā is unconscious.
Mahāmāyā is multiple in nature.
Unconsciousness and multiplicity entail perishability.
mukta-m0-p08-v188.inference: Therefore Mahāmāyā's perishability is well ascertained.

mukta-m0-p08-v189.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v189.question: Why must Mahāmāyā be all-pervading in producing enjoyment for souls?
premises: Souls are infinite in number.
Mahāmāyā acts for the sake of enjoyment.
Providing enjoyment to infinite souls requires pervasiveness.
mukta-m0-p08-v189.inference: Therefore Mahāmāyā is all-pervading because it produces enjoyment for infinite souls.

mukta-m0-p08-v190.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v190.question: In what manner does Mahāmāyā undergo transformation without changing wholly?
premises: Mahāmāyā undergoes transformation.
It does not transform in its whole nature.
The ghee-worm maxim illustrates transformation by one part.
mukta-m0-p08-v190.inference: Therefore Mahāmāyā should be understood to transform by one part, not wholly.

mukta-m0-p08-v191.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v191.question: Where do creation, maintenance, and dissolution abide in relation to Mahāmāyā?
premises: Creation, maintenance, and dissolution are attributed to Mahāmāyā.
These processes are not external to its nature.
They are declared to abide in its own self.
mukta-m0-p08-v191.inference: Therefore creation, maintenance, and dissolution abide within Mahāmāyā itself.

mukta-m0-p08-v192.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v192.question: How is Mahāmāyā's material causality reconciled without contradiction?
premises: Mahāmāyā functions as a means of enjoyment.
It is also described as material cause.
These roles are presented as compatible.
mukta-m0-p08-v192.inference: Therefore there is no contradiction in Mahāmāyā being material cause as a means of enjoyment.

mukta-m0-p08-v193.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v193.question: How is dissolution defined in relation to creation and maintenance?
premises: Creation and maintenance have been declared.
Dissolution is the remaining process.
Dissolution is explained as the reversal of creation.
mukta-m0-p08-v193.inference: Therefore dissolution is the reverse of creation.

mukta-m0-p08-v194.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v194.question: What does dissolution mean as reabsorption into respective causes?
premises: Dissolution follows the reverse order of creation.
Effects return to their own causes.
This return is called reabsorption.
mukta-m0-p08-v194.inference: Therefore dissolution means reabsorption into respective causes in reverse order of creation.

mukta-m0-p08-v195.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v195.question: By what means do souls experience objects made of Māyā?
premises: Souls have objects of enjoyment.
Those objects are made of Māyā.
The means of enjoyment arise from Māyā.
mukta-m0-p08-v195.inference: Therefore souls experience Māyā-made objects through means born of Māyā.

mukta-m0-p08-v196.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v196.question: Why must limited knowledge and similar properties be inferred rather than directly seen?
premises: Limited knowledge and similar properties are under discussion.
These properties are not directly perceived.
Non-perception requires another basis for affirmation.
mukta-m0-p08-v196.inference: Therefore limited knowledge and similar properties are established from non-perception rather than direct sight.

mukta-m0-p08-v197.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v197.question: Why does the soul become an object when covered by impurity?
premises: The soul's all-knowledge and all-action are covered by impurity.
Being covered makes the soul subject to experience.
Subjection to experience entails objecthood.
mukta-m0-p08-v197.inference: Therefore the soul has objecthood because its all-knowledge and all-action are covered by impurity.

mukta-m0-p08-v198.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v198.question: What would cause the soul's attachment to enjoyments if no impurity existed?
premises: The Svāyaṃbhuva scripture raises a hypothetical case.
In that case the soul has no impurity.
Attachment to enjoyments would still need a cause.
mukta-m0-p08-v198.inference: Therefore attachment to enjoyments implies the presence of impurity in the soul.

mukta-m0-p08-v199.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v199.question: How does karma performed in another birth produce results for embodied beings?
premises: Karma can be performed in another birth.
Such karma yields fruits such as birth.
These fruits pertain to embodied beings.
mukta-m0-p08-v199.inference: Therefore karma done in another birth gives birth and other fruits to embodied beings.

mukta-m0-p08-v200.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p08-v200.question: Can the power of karma to produce birth and other results operate without impurity?
premises: Karma possesses a power that produces birth and other results.
This productive power of karma is under consideration as a cause of embodied experience.
The operation of this power is negated in the absence of impurity.
mukta-m0-p08-v200.inference: Therefore, the power of karma to produce birth and other results requires impurity as a necessary condition.

mukta-m0-p09-v201.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v201.question: Why do karma acquisition and its experience apply only to the impurity-endowed soul?
premises: Performance of action is not observed in all cases
Karma acquisition presupposes an agent subject to impurity
Experience of karma follows from such acquisition
mukta-m0-p09-v201.inference: Therefore karma acquisition and its experience are applicable only to the soul endowed with impurity.

mukta-m0-p09-v202.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v202.question: What role does karma play if the soul’s object-directedness is already singular?
premises: Object-directedness may be admitted as single for that soul
A single object-directedness does not require karma for its existence
Karma would be superfluous in that case
mukta-m0-p09-v202.inference: Therefore karma is not needed merely to account for that object-directedness.

mukta-m0-p09-v203.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v203.question: Do isolated souls exist without karma while their knowledge remains obscured?
premises: Some souls are described as kevalins
These souls are deprived of karma
Their knowledge is consumed or obstructed
mukta-m0-p09-v203.inference: Therefore isolated souls can exist without karma in a state of obscured knowledge.

mukta-m0-p09-v204.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v204.question: What is identified as the cause in the soul’s connection with māyā?
premises: The context concerns the soul’s association with māyā
A causal factor is being specified
The statement summarizes that causal claim
mukta-m0-p09-v204.inference: Thus the meaning is that connection with māyā is the cause.

mukta-m0-p09-v205.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v205.question: Why is the soul before creation described as partless yet possessing cognition and action?
premises: Before creation the soul is without kalā and similar adjuncts
The soul is still held to possess cognition and action
This condition requires explanation
mukta-m0-p09-v205.inference: Because the soul inherently possesses cognition and action even before creation, it is described as partless yet endowed with those qualities.

mukta-m0-p09-v206.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v206.question: Why must impurity be admitted to explain the soul’s connection with kalā?
premises: The soul comes into connection with kalā
This connection cannot be explained otherwise
An obscuring cause must account for that limitation
mukta-m0-p09-v206.inference: Therefore impurity must be admitted for that soul.

mukta-m0-p09-v207.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v207.question: Why are the individual self’s cognition and action held to be all-encompassing in scope?
premises: The individual self is regarded as omnipresent
Cognition and action belong to that self
Omnipresence implies unrestricted scope
mukta-m0-p09-v207.inference: Therefore the self’s cognition and action are held to extend to all objects.

mukta-m0-p09-v208.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v208.question: Why are the individual self’s cognition and action not manifest despite their universal scope?
premises: The self’s cognition and action are in principle all-encompassing
Manifestation requires manifesting adjuncts such as kalā
Such manifestors are absent in that condition
mukta-m0-p09-v208.inference: Therefore the self’s cognition and action are not manifest.

mukta-m0-p09-v209.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v209.question: What characteristics define the impurity’s connection with the beginningless soul?
premises: The connection is between two beginningless realities
Impurity is common to souls
Impurity is imperishable
mukta-m0-p09-v209.inference: Therefore impurity stands in a beginningless, common, and imperishable connection.

mukta-m0-p09-v210.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v210.question: Why must impurity be admitted as eternal on the basis of its beginningless connection?
premises: Impurity’s connection with the soul is beginningless
What is beginningless in this relation is not temporally produced
Such a principle must be admitted in doctrine
mukta-m0-p09-v210.inference: Therefore impurity must indeed be admitted as eternal.

mukta-m0-p09-v211.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v211.question: Was the individual self stainless prior to the arising of great delusion?
premises: Great delusion is said to arise at some point
A prior condition of the soul is being considered
Stainlessness would mean absence of impurity
mukta-m0-p09-v211.inference: The verse presents the view that this individual self was stainless before the arising of great delusion.
uncertainties: Whether this states an accepted position or a view to be refuted depends on context.

mukta-m0-p09-v212.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v212.question: Why must the connection between impurity and the self be admitted as beginningless?
premises: A prior stainless state of the self is problematic for explaining bondage
The relation of impurity to the self requires a stable account
A beginningless connection avoids that difficulty
mukta-m0-p09-v212.inference: Therefore the connection of impurity with the self must be admitted as beginningless.

mukta-m0-p09-v213.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v213.question: What consequence follows if the connection between soul and impurity is accepted as having a beginning?
premises: One may propose that the soul-impurity connection has a beginning
A beginning implies a cause or initiating condition
The verse raises this as a challenge to that proposal
mukta-m0-p09-v213.inference: If the connection of soul and impurity is taken to have a beginning, its cause must be accounted for.

mukta-m0-p09-v214.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v214.question: Why would accepting a beginningless connection as causeless make the connection with kalā causeless as well?
premises: If the soul-impurity connection is said to arise without cause, causality is abandoned
The connection with kalā is another such relation requiring explanation
The same reasoning would apply to it
mukta-m0-p09-v214.inference: Then the connection with kalā would also have to be accepted as without cause.

mukta-m0-p09-v215.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v215.question: Can a beginningless connection between beginningless entities be coherently regarded as perishable?
premises: The connection is proposed as beginningless on both sides
Perishability implies an end and thus temporal limitation
The verse tests the coherence of combining these claims
mukta-m0-p09-v215.inference: If the connection is beginningless, it cannot coherently be accepted as perishable.

mukta-m0-p09-v216.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v216.question: How are the powers of impurity distributed and what function do they perform for each soul?
premises: Impurity operates through distinct powers
These powers are fixed for each individual soul
Their function is to obstruct the soul’s qualities
mukta-m0-p09-v216.inference: Therefore impurity has individually fixed powers that obstruct the qualities of each soul.

mukta-m0-p09-v217.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v217.question: What specific soul qualities are obstructed by impurity’s powers according to prior demonstration?
premises: The soul’s essential qualities are cognition and action
Impurity’s powers obstruct these qualities
This point has already been shown earlier
mukta-m0-p09-v217.inference: Therefore the obstruction of the soul’s cognition-and-action qualities by impurity has been previously established.

mukta-m0-p09-v218.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v218.question: What undesirable consequence would follow if impurity were not individually fixed for each soul?
premises: Impurity’s obstructing powers are held to be fixed per soul
If not fixed individually, removal would affect all alike
Liberation would then occur for all conscious beings simultaneously
mukta-m0-p09-v218.inference: Therefore impurity must be individually fixed to avoid simultaneous liberation of all.

mukta-m0-p09-v219.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v219.question: How should the modifications mentioned in Svāyambhuva and related scripture be understood?
premises: Scriptural passages such as the Svāyambhuva are cited
These passages refer to certain modifications
The doctrinal conclusion qualifies their status
mukta-m0-p09-v219.inference: Therefore those modifications are to be known as adventitious.

mukta-m0-p09-v220.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v220.question: Are the five modifications such as pride proper to the soul’s object-directedness?
premises: Object-directedness is attributed to the soul
Five modifications beginning with pride are considered
Their intrinsic appropriateness to that state is questioned
mukta-m0-p09-v220.inference: Therefore the five modifications such as pride are not proper to object-directedness.

mukta-m0-p09-v221.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v221.question: How can the presence of those modifications be reconciled without contradiction?
premises: The modifications are not proper to the soul’s object-directedness itself
Impurity may serve as their material cause
A material-cause explanation can remove contradiction
mukta-m0-p09-v221.inference: Therefore there is no contradiction if they are explained as having impurity as their material cause.

mukta-m0-p09-v222.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v222.question: Is it proper to explain these modifications merely as manifestations from connection with means of experience?
premises: One might claim the modifications are manifested through means of experience
This explanation treats them as externally revealed only
The verse evaluates that explanation as inadequate
mukta-m0-p09-v222.inference: Therefore it is not proper to explain them merely by connection with the means of experience.

mukta-m0-p09-v223.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v223.question: How does the opponent distinguish pride and similar states from the modifications of the guṇas?
premises: Pride and similar states are under discussion
Modifications of the guṇas are another explanatory category
The opponent asserts a distinction between them
mukta-m0-p09-v223.inference: According to you, pride and the rest are indeed distinct from the modifications of the guṇas.
uncertainties: The token 'ntu' is taken as a contrastive particle in this context.

mukta-m0-p09-v224.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v224.question: How are the five modifications classified according to the three guṇas in sequence?
premises: Five modifications are under discussion
They are distributed among tamas, sattva, and rajas
The distribution follows a specific order
mukta-m0-p09-v224.inference: Therefore the five modifications are classified in order as two tāmasa, one sāttvika, and two rājasa.

mukta-m0-p09-v225.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p09-v225.question: On what ontological ground must the modifications in question be denied existence rather than denied mere distinction from their source?
premises: The modifications are not distinct from those modes specified in the preceding verses.
Modifications are only posited in relation to a root as their source.
If no distinct modifications of the root are admitted, no such modifications can exist.
mukta-m0-p09-v225.inference: Since the modifications are not distinct from the previously named modes and cannot stand as distinct from the root, they do not exist.
uncertainties: The precise anaphoric reach of ābhyaḥ depends strictly on v223–v224 and is not recoverable from this verse alone.

mukta-m0-p08-v176.plain_english: Because the individual self has changeability and similar properties, and because scripture also contradicts it, such a view cannot hold for the individual self.

mukta-m0-p08-v177.plain_english: Thus the individual self is not all-pervading, not momentary, not one, and not inert in nature.
mukta-m0-p08-v177.sanskrit_cite: nāvyāpako na kṣaṇiko naiko nāpi jaḍātmakaḥ (vi0 6 7) iti ca

mukta-m0-p08-v178.plain_english: Other groups among the principles are enjoyers and serve as grounds of pleasure.

mukta-m0-p08-v179.plain_english: This means they are the places of enjoyment for transmigrating beings.

mukta-m0-p08-v180.plain_english: The range from hell up to the world of truth is governed by the Kālāhāṭaka lords.

mukta-m0-p08-v181.plain_english: And the Śatarudra lord also governs together with five octads.

mukta-m0-p08-v182.plain_english: But Kalā is governed by the Maṇḍalins.

mukta-m0-p08-v183.plain_english: And one should place them in sequence in the intellect.

mukta-m0-p08-v184.plain_english: But when the state of the qualities has not yet been attained, it should be placed in the pure summit of the qualities.

mukta-m0-p08-v185.plain_english: The row of worlds of Krodheśvara and the other Rudras abides in Pradhāna.

mukta-m0-p08-v186.plain_english: Mahāmāyā is the seed of the world, a productive power, and unconscious.

mukta-m0-p08-v187.plain_english: This Mahāmāyā is endowed with many variegated powers.

mukta-m0-p08-v188.plain_english: Because it is unconscious and multiple, its perishability is well established.

mukta-m0-p08-v189.plain_english: Because souls are infinite, it is all-pervading and acts for the sake of their enjoyment.

mukta-m0-p08-v190.plain_english: It undergoes transformation, but not in its whole nature; by the maxim of the ghee-worm, it should be understood to transform by one part.

mukta-m0-p08-v191.plain_english: Creation, maintenance, and dissolution of that Mahāmāyā are declared to abide within its own nature.

mukta-m0-p08-v192.plain_english: As a means of enjoyment it is the material cause; thus there is no contradiction.

mukta-m0-p08-v193.plain_english: Creation and maintenance have been explained; dissolution is the reversal of creation.

mukta-m0-p08-v194.plain_english: This means reabsorption into their respective causes in the reverse order of creation.

mukta-m0-p08-v195.plain_english: For souls, the object of enjoyment is made of Māyā and is experienced indeed through means born of Māyā.

mukta-m0-p08-v196.plain_english: Also because limited knowledge and such properties are not directly perceived.

mukta-m0-p08-v197.plain_english: Because, when covered by impurity, its all-knowledge and all-action are obscured, it becomes an object.

mukta-m0-p08-v198.plain_english: In the revered Svāyaṃbhuva it is asked: if the soul had no impurity, what would cause its attachment to enjoyments?

mukta-m0-p08-v199.plain_english: Karma performed in another birth gives rise to birth and other fruits for human beings.

mukta-m0-p08-v200.plain_english: The power of karma that produces birth and so forth does not operate without impurity.
mukta-m0-p08-v200.sanskrit_cite: janmādijanikā śaktiḥ karmaṇo na malaṃ vinā

mukta-m0-p09-v201.plain_english: Because the performance of action is not seen otherwise, the acquisition of karma and its experience apply only to the soul that is endowed with impurity.
mukta-m0-p09-v201.sanskrit_cite: karmānuṣṭhānādarśanācca malayuktasyaiva karmārjanaṃ tadbhogo vā upayujyate

mukta-m0-p09-v202.plain_english: Indeed, let that soul’s object-directedness be one; what use is there for that karma?
mukta-m0-p09-v202.sanskrit_cite: viṣayitvaṃ hi tasyaikamastu kiṃ tena karmaṇā

mukta-m0-p09-v203.plain_english: There are isolated souls, deprived of karma, whose knowledge is consumed.

mukta-m0-p09-v204.plain_english: The meaning is: the cause lies in connection with māyā.

mukta-m0-p09-v205.plain_english: Because before creation the soul is without parts yet possesses the qualities of cognition and action.

mukta-m0-p09-v206.plain_english: The meaning is that, because connection with kalā would otherwise be inexplicable, impurity must be admitted for that soul.

mukta-m0-p09-v207.plain_english: Because the individual self is omnipresent, its cognition and action are held to have all objects as their scope.

mukta-m0-p09-v208.plain_english: Because there are no manifestors such as kalā and the rest, that soul’s cognition and action are not manifest.

mukta-m0-p09-v209.plain_english: Impurity is in a beginningless connection with the beginningless, is common, and is imperishable.

mukta-m0-p09-v210.plain_english: For that very reason, impurity must indeed be admitted as eternal.

mukta-m0-p09-v211.plain_english: Before the arising of great delusion, this individual self was stainless.

mukta-m0-p09-v212.plain_english: The connection of impurity with the self must be admitted to be beginningless.

mukta-m0-p09-v213.plain_english: O wise ones, if the connection between the soul and impurity is accepted as having a beginning—

mukta-m0-p09-v214.plain_english: Then, if that connection is without cause, the connection with kalā would also be without cause.

mukta-m0-p09-v215.plain_english: And if a beginningless connection between beginningless entities is accepted, can it be perishable?

mukta-m0-p09-v216.plain_english: And its powers, fixed for each soul, obstruct the soul’s qualities.

mukta-m0-p09-v217.plain_english: They obstruct the soul’s quality whose nature is knowledge and action; and this has indeed been shown previously.
mukta-m0-p09-v217.sanskrit_cite: ātmaguṇasya jñānakriyātmano rodhikāḥ etacca prāgeva darśitam

mukta-m0-p09-v218.plain_english: Otherwise, all conscious beings would be liberated simultaneously.

mukta-m0-p09-v219.plain_english: Thus, according to the revered Svāyambhuva and other scriptures, they are to be known as indeed adventitious.

mukta-m0-p09-v220.plain_english: The five modifications of object-directedness, beginning with pride, are not proper.

mukta-m0-p09-v221.plain_english: But there is no contradiction, since they have impurity as their material cause.

mukta-m0-p09-v222.plain_english: It is not proper to say that they are manifested merely through connection with the means of experience.

mukta-m0-p09-v223.plain_english: But according to you, pride and the rest are indeed distinct from the modifications of the guṇas.

mukta-m0-p09-v224.plain_english: In due order, two are tāmasa, one is sāttvika, and two are rājasa.

mukta-m0-p09-v225.plain_english: The modifications are not distinct from these; therefore, as modifications distinct from the root, they do not exist.
mukta-m0-p09-v225.sanskrit_cite: ābhyo bhinnā na mūlasya vṛttayo'to na santi tāḥ

essence: Therefore views incompatible with changeability and scripture cannot correctly describe the individual self.
Therefore these characterizations do not properly define the individual self.
Therefore some groups of principles function as enjoying grounds.
Therefore those grounds are the places of enjoyment for transmigrating beings.
Therefore the Kālāhāṭaka lords govern the worlds from hell up to the world of truth.
mukta-m0-p08.essence_source: derived from argmap inferences (machine-proposed; assessor review outstanding)

essence: Therefore karma acquisition and its experience are applicable only to the soul endowed with impurity.
Therefore karma is not needed merely to account for that object-directedness.
Therefore isolated souls can exist without karma in a state of obscured knowledge.
Thus the meaning is that connection with māyā is the cause.
Because the soul inherently possesses cognition and action even before creation, it is described as partless yet endowed with those qualities.
